summary: Russian attacks continue across Ukraine with drone and missile strikes targeting infrastructure and civilian areas. Ukraine faces critical shortages of Patriot PAC-3 missiles while defending against ongoing aerial threats. Multiple regions report damage to civilian infrastructure including water systems, energy facilities, and residential buildings.
key_points: Ukraine reports extreme difficulty obtaining PAC-3 missiles for Patriot systems, with Foreign Minister Sybiga stating 'We're literally fighting for every missile.' (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32248)
Marganets, Nikopol, Pokrov, and Tomakivka in Dnepropetrovsk region have been without water for five days due to an accident on the main water pipeline. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32228)
Russian pilots dropped two FAB-3000 air bombs with UMPK guidance system on a Ukrainian military crossing in Orekhov, Zaporozhye region. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32235)

Over 400,000 square meters of warehouses and logistics facilities have been destroyed by Russian forces since July 2026, targeting companies including Fozzy Group, Rozetka, and Epicenter. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32250)
Chernigov residents are using anti-drone nets to protect gas stations from Russian drones. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32243)
Norway is prepared to provide air defense systems to Ukraine, with President Zelenskyy thanking Norway for readiness to help with air defense materials. (Source: @UkraineNow/83261)
Multiple drone attacks reported across Ukraine including reactive drones targeting northern Odishyna toward Voznesen'sk and southern Dnipro region. (Source: @kpszsu/71810, @kpszsu/71813)
Tax Service will transfer data on Ukrainian men aged 18-60 to the Ministry of Defense for the military registry 'Obereh'. (Source: @UkraineNow/83256)

sections.executive_summary: Russian attacks continue across Ukraine with drone and missile strikes targeting infrastructure and civilian areas. President Zelenskyy confirmed Norway's readiness to provide air defense systems, thanking the country for preparedness in supplying anti-ballistic missile defense materials. (Source: @UkraineNow/83261)

Approximately 16,000 foreign volunteers from 72 countries are currently defending Ukraine, with nearly 40% coming from Latin American nations, according to the Military Ombudsman. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23722)

Education reforms include a 20% salary increase for teachers from September 1, 2026, with student stipends doubling and free meals provided to all schoolchildren despite Russian attacks on printing facilities and warehouses. (Source: @UkraineNow/83263)
Viktor Yushchenko has been appointed head of the supervisory board of the National Holodomor Genocide Museum. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32251)

Psychologist Natalia Kholodenko stated that while it is safe to freely express hatred toward Russians, speaking about human rights violations, 60,000 soldiers waiting for prosthetics, or people not surviving at the front is not safe. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32229)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces maintain aggressive offensive posture across multiple fronts with increased drone and missile activity targeting Ukrainian infrastructure and civilian populations. Critical shortages of Patriot PAC-3 missiles severely limit Ukraine's ability to defend against aerial threats, creating vulnerability in key defensive sectors. The destruction of over 400,000 square meters of logistics facilities since July 2026 indicates sustained targeting of supply chains and commercial infrastructure. Norwegian support for air defense systems represents a significant capability enhancement that could offset current missile shortages. Foreign volunteer forces from 72 countries provide additional defensive capacity, though their integration requires careful coordination with national forces.
sections.regional_response: Norway has offered air defense support to Ukraine, with President Zelenskyy expressing gratitude for readiness to supply anti-ballistic missile defense materials. Poland has formally addressed vandalism of Ukrainian Insurgent Army graves, with Ukrainian Embassy condemning attempts to escalate historical disputes into modern conflicts. International community continues supporting Ukraine through military aid and diplomatic backing despite Russian claims of Western neglect of Kyiv's terrorism. Education reforms proceed with teacher salary increases and free meals for students despite ongoing Russian attacks on educational infrastructure. Tax data sharing with military represents expanded conscription capabilities for sustained defense operations.
sections.intelligence_notes: Russian military operations demonstrate coordinated multi-front attacks with emphasis on infrastructure degradation and civilian targeting. Ukrainian defensive measures include improvised solutions like anti-drone nets and systematic data collection for military registration. Foreign volunteer integration shows international solidarity but requires enhanced legal protections and support mechanisms. Norwegian air defense contributions could significantly alter regional balance if delivered promptly. Historical memory operations by both sides indicate information warfare component alongside kinetic operations.
